content.text:
No Critical or Important findings in the scoped additions.

Minor observations:

- `nova/evaluation.py:120-125,282-284`: absent-capability cases receive recall/precision 1 when nothing is retrieved, then contribute to the same aggregate as positive cases. This is a defensible scoring convention, but aggregate “retrieval_recall” includes successful abstention; document it or log positive-case recall and abstention accuracy separately.
- `nova/evaluation.py:281-284`: all metrics use an unweighted case mean, including counts (`budget_violations`, `discovery_calls`) and per-case peaks. Thus MLflow’s `budget_violations` is mean violations per case and `peak_schema_tokens` is mean case peak. Labels or separate sum/max metrics would make dashboards clearer. JSON retains the underlying evidence and exit handling still detects any violation.

Verified separation of ranked retrieval from actual availability, retained paraphrase misses, independent fresh catalogs per case, full-schema control, budget-blocked retrieval evidence, split filtering, and backward-compatible default baseline reporting. Tests now include baseline/all CLI coverage.

Validation: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_evaluation.py --no-cov -q` → **18 passed**. Ordinary targeted pytest also passed all 18 tests but failed the repository-wide coverage threshold; `uv run` initially hit the restricted uv cache.

Declined to judge: live agent task completion, argument correctness, provider billing/cost, production behavior, actual MLflow persistence (mocked in these tests), and whether fixtures remained unchanged after earlier heldout results (historical provenance unavailable from current untracked files). No edits made.
